events.text:
**Go to Grand Haven.** I'd expect it to be the best of the four this week, but it's a modest edge and the newest reports are 6 days old (2023-08-30).

| Port | My rating (0-4) | Latest boat report |
|---|---|---|
| Grand Haven | **3 (good)** | Rated 3 |
| South Haven | **2 (average)** | Rated 0, but the text says "pretty good" |
| Muskegon | **1 (below average)** | Rated 0 |
| St. Joseph | **1 (below average)** | Not rated |

**How to fish Grand Haven**
- Start in 40–80 ft of water, using glow or chrome J-plugs and white flasher/flies (Grand Haven, 2023-08-30).
- If that fades, move out. Earlier reports had fish 40–100 ft down in 70–180 ft of water, on glow spoons, glow plugs and meat rigs (Grand Haven, 2023-08-16, 2023-08-23).
- The 2023-08-30 report didn't give a fish depth. The 40–100 ft depths come from the earlier weeks.

**Evidence by port**
- **Grand Haven:**
  - Boat fishing was good on 2023-08-30. It was good on 08-16 and 08-09 and below that on 08-23. The 08-23 report said "slow" in 90–180 ft, with the best action 45–100 ft down.
  - Pier anglers only caught a few salmon (Grand Haven, 2023-08-30).
- **South Haven:**
  - The 2023-08-30 report is contradictory. It was coded 0 (slow), yet the text says "when boat anglers made it out, the salmon fishing was pretty good." It also says the Black River trolling was very slow.
  - Fish were caught in 90–120 ft, best around 100 ft, on meat rigs, rotators and flies (South Haven, 2023-08-30).
  - The week before was tough, with fish "very scattered" around 100 ft (South Haven, 2023-08-23).
  - Weather seems to have limited effort that week, so the 0 may understate the fishing.
- **Muskegon:**
  - Slow on both 2023-08-30 and 08-23. On 08-30, the fish that were caught came 55–100 ft down in 70–130 ft of water, on glow spoons, meat rigs and J-plugs (Muskegon, 2023-08-30).
  - It was good as recently as 08-16 (Muskegon, 2023-08-16).
- **St. Joseph:**
  - Few boats got out because of poor weather, so there's little information. They targeted 90–100 ft (St. Joseph, 2023-08-30).
  - Earlier weeks were slow to below average: 0 on 08-23 and 1 on 08-16 (St. Joseph, 2023-08-23, 2023-08-16).

**Water temperature**
- The buoy summaries for the week before today show surface water averaging 63 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon, 68 F at South Haven and 71 F at St. Joseph. The Grand Haven and Muskegon buoy is up 12 F over the week (2023-09-05 buoy summaries).
- Live data was unavailable, so I have no wind forecast and no modeled cold-layer depth. Check the marine forecast yourself before you go.

**History (earlier seasons, same time of year)**
- In early September 2022, Grand Haven was fair to good in 40–120 ft and 55–110 ft down (Grand Haven, 2022-09-07, 2022-09-14).
- South Haven was average to good, with fish around 110 ft (South Haven, 2022-09-07, 2022-09-14).
- Muskegon was average, then below average (Muskegon, 2022-09-07, 2022-09-14). St. Joseph was below average (St. Joseph, 2022-09-07, 2022-09-14).
- That's the same pecking order I'm using now.

**My read**
- Grand Haven's good report at 40–80 ft came right after the buoy's sharp 11 F drop, which is the upwelling sign. I'd expect cool water to have pulled salmon closer to shore there. Michigan Sea Grant guidance says this kind of upwelling brings salmon toward shore.
- The 12 F rebound since then could scatter that shallow bite. That's why I'd rate Grand Haven 3 rather than 4, and why I'd move deeper if the shallows go quiet.
- South Haven is the fallback. I'd put it at 2 because the text is better than its 0 code.
- I'd expect Muskegon to stay slow unless a fresh upwelling pushes fish back in, as it did on 08-16.
- I'd expect St. Joseph to be the least reliable, because it has the warmest water and few reports.
